import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The SDKs are thin clients for the [public API](/build/api-overview/): one method per endpoint, typed responses and a single error type. They do the routine work for you: the base URL, encoding identifiers, timeouts and turning error responses into exceptions.

The SDKs **add no checks of their own**. Every result comes from the API and means exactly what the API page for that endpoint says. Anything the SDKs do not cover, you can call over HTTP.

## What you get

| | TypeScript | Python |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package | [`@didis/client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@didis/client) 0.2.5 | [`didis-py`](https://pypi.org/project/didis-py/) 0.2.5 (import `didis`) |
| Source | [did-is/didis-js](https://github.com/did-is/didis-js) | [did-is/didis-py](https://github.com/did-is/didis-py) |
| Runtime | Any runtime with `fetch`: Node 18+, Deno, Bun, browsers, edge. Zero dependencies, ESM. | Python 3.11+, `httpx`. Sync `DidisClient` and async `AsyncDidisClient`. |
| Responses | Typed objects | Plain `dict`s typed with `TypedDict` (`didis.types`) |
| Timeout | `new DidisClient({ timeoutMs })`, default 30 000 | `DidisClient(timeout=…)`, default 30.0 seconds |

## What they do not do

- **Retries beyond `Retry-After`.** From 0.2.4 the SDKs wait for `Retry-After` and retry a `429` or `503` up to twice (at most 10 seconds per wait). Other errors raise `DidisError` at once. Pass `retry: false` (TypeScript) or `retry=False` (Python) to handle every retry yourself (see [Errors and rate limits](/build/errors/#retrying-in-the-sdks)).
- **Directory and claims.** These endpoints have no SDK method; call them over HTTP (see the [API reference](/reference/api/#directory-and-claims)).
- **Gateway middleware.** There is no ready-made proxy or framework plugin. To guard individual tool handlers, use the SDK guard; [Guard agent tools](/build/guard-tools/#use-with-mcp-and-agent-frameworks) shows how with MCP clients, LangChain and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

## Install

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```bash
npm install @didis/client
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```bash
pip install didis-py
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Rust">
```bash
# No official Rust SDK: use any HTTP client.
cargo add reqwest --features json
cargo add serde_json
cargo add tokio --features full
```
</TabItem>

## Basic use

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```ts
import { DidisClient, DidisError } from "@didis/client";

const didis = new DidisClient();

try {
  const r = await didis.resolve("did:web:did.is");
  console.log(r.verdict.headline);
  for (const d of r.dimensions) console.log(d.label, d.state);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof DidisError) console.log(e.status, e.problem.code, e.problem.detail);
  else throw e;
}
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```python
from didis import DidisClient, DidisError

with DidisClient() as didis:
    try:
        r = didis.resolve("did:web:did.is")
        print(r["verdict"]["headline"])
        for d in r["dimensions"]:
            print(d["label"], d["state"])
    except DidisError as e:
        print(e.status, e.problem.get("code"), e.problem.get("detail"))
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Rust">
```rust
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let r: serde_json::Value = reqwest::get("https://did.is/api/v1/resolve/did%3Aweb%3Adid.is")
        .await?
        .error_for_status()?
        .json()
        .await?;
    println!("{}", r["verdict"]["headline"]);
    Ok(())
}
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Async Python:

```python
import asyncio
from didis import AsyncDidisClient

async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncDidisClient() as didis:
        r = await didis.resolve("did:web:did.is")
        print(r["verdict"]["outcome"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

In Rust, percent-encode the identifier once, and on non-2xx responses read the RFC 9457 problem body and the `Retry-After` header yourself (see [Errors](/build/errors/)).

## Using a project API key

Without a key, every call uses the anonymous public API and its per-client budget. With a project API key from the [console](/app/accounts/) (SDK 0.2.5 or later), four methods count against your team's monthly allowance instead: `inspectMcp`, `inspectA2a`, `authorize` and `verifyDelegation` (`inspect_mcp`, `inspect_a2a`, `authorize`, `verify_delegation` in Python). The results are the same as without a key.

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```ts
import { DidisClient } from "@didis/client";

const didis = new DidisClient({ apiKey: process.env.DID_IS_API_KEY });

const decision = await didis.authorize(chain, "payments:refund");
const usage = await didis.usage();
console.log(usage.expensiveUsed, "of", usage.expensiveLimit, "used in", usage.period);
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```python
import os
from didis import DidisClient

with DidisClient(api_key=os.environ["DID_IS_API_KEY"]) as didis:
    decision = didis.authorize(chain, "payments:refund")
    usage = didis.usage()
    print(usage["expensiveUsed"], "of", usage["expensiveLimit"], "used in", usage["period"])
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

- **The key is sent only for those calls** and for `usage()`. All other methods, and `verifyDelegation` with `register: true`, keep using the public API without the key.
- **Keep the key server-side.** Read it from an environment variable or a secret store. Never put it in browser or mobile code.
- **No double billing.** Each call carries a fresh idempotency key, and the automatic retries reuse it, so a retried request is counted once.
- **`usage()`** returns this month's allowance for the whole team (all projects share it): `period`, plus `Used`, `Reserved`, `Limit` and `Remaining` for the `standard` and `expensive` pools. It needs a key and is not counted.
- **When the allowance is used up,** these calls raise `DidisError` with status `429` and code `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` until the next month or a plan change. Retrying does not help. Remove the key to fall back to the anonymous public API.

The team's owners also get an email at 80% and at 100% of each monthly allowance (see [Accounts, projects and plans](/app/accounts/#usage-and-alerts)).

## Reading the result

| What happens | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The method returns | The API answered 2xx. | Read the result fields, for example `verdict` or `status`. |
| `DidisError`, `status` 429 or 503 | Budget used up, or service busy. `problem.retryAfter` holds the `Retry-After` value. | Wait that long, then retry. |
| `DidisError`, other 4xx | The request itself is wrong, or the method or feature is not supported. | Fix the request; `problem.code` says why. Do not retry unchanged. |
| `DidisError`, 5xx | DID.is or the remote host failed. | Retry later. |
| Timeout | No answer within the client timeout. | Retry later, or raise the timeout. |

## Methods

| TypeScript | Python | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `health()` | `health()` | `GET /health` |
| `resolve(did, { noCache })` | `resolve(did, no_cache=…)` | `GET /v1/resolve/{did}` |
| `resolveW3c(did)` | `resolve_w3c(did)` | `GET /1.0/identifiers/{did}` |
| `dereference(didUrl)` | `dereference(did_url)` | `GET /v1/dereference/{didUrl}` |
| `stream(did)` | `stream(did)` | `GET /v1/stream/{did}` |
| `history(did)` | `history(did)` | `GET /v1/history/{did}` |
| `diff(did, from?, to?)` | `diff(did, …)` | `GET /v1/diff/{did}` |
| `graph(did)` | `graph(did)` | `GET /v1/graph/{did}` |
| `verifyCredential(vc, { expectedAudience })` | `verify_credential(vc, …)` | `POST /v1/credentials/verify` |
| `evaluatePolicy(did, policy, vc?)` | `evaluate_policy(did, policy, credential=None)` | `POST /v1/policies/evaluate` |
| `inspectMcp(endpoint)` | `inspect_mcp(endpoint)` | `GET /v1/mcp/inspect` |
| `inspectA2a(url)` | `inspect_a2a(url)` | `GET /v1/a2a/inspect` |
| `verifyDelegation(chain, { trustedRoots, register })` | `verify_delegation(chain, trusted_roots=…, register=…)` | `POST /v1/agents/verify-delegation` |
| `authorize(chain, tool, { trustedRoots })` | `authorize(chain, tool, trusted_roots=…)` | `POST /v1/agents/authorize` |
| `verifyTool(agent, tool, root?)` | `verify_tool(agent, tool, root=None)` | `GET /v1/agents/verify-tool` |
| `fastVerifyDid(did)` | `fast_verify_did(did)` | `GET /v1/fast-verify/did/{did}` |
| `fastVerifyJws(jws, relationship?)` | `fast_verify_jws(jws, relationship=None)` | `POST /v1/fast-verify/jws` |
| `usage()` (needs a key) | `usage()` (needs `api_key`) | Team allowance this month |
| `verifyCustomerMonitorSignature(…)` | `verify_customer_monitor_signature(…)` | [Webhook signatures](/build/webhooks/) |

## No CLI

There is no published DID.is command-line tool. Use `curl` or the SDKs.
